description:
Advances: specled.package

Two pre-existing findings surfaced by cold verification of specled_-vk0 (epic specled_-233, 2026-07-26). NEITHER was introduced by that ticket — both reproduce at its base a6954fc9 — so both were correctly left out of it.

FINDING 1 — stale absolute counts in the ADR. .spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md cites absolute corpus occurrence counts for the four unusable stems as detector_ 69, requirement_ 45, decision_ 24, verification_ 39. Measured 2026-07-26 against the real 97-file corpus: 78, 110, 46, 39. Only verification_ still matches. Guidance-only counting gives 24/24/8/1, which matches neither, so the numbers cannot be recovered by reinterpreting the corpus.

Why it matters and why it is low priority: the ADR's LOAD-BEARING claim is comparative, not absolute — that the four stems collide with real non-code identifiers while the deferred narrow stems (surface_target_, scenario_cover_, meta_field_) collide with nothing. That comparative claim reproduces EXACTLY (5, 11, 12 and 19 distinct non-code collisions respectively; zero occurrences for the deferred stems; spec_requirement_ 12 and invalid_id_ 1, each match being the stem's own real code). So the argument is sound and only its illustrative figures have drifted. Fix: either refresh the four numbers, or reword them as approximations, or drop them and keep the comparative statement — the last is probably best, since absolute counts in an ADR will drift again by construction.

FINDING 2 — mirror union masks a single-file decommission. test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs's two-way mirror derives the implementation code set as a UNION over the 10 files in @implementation_code_files. Consequence: a code removed from its EMITTING detector while a literal survives elsewhere (typically lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex @per_code_defaults) keeps the mirror green. Reproduced: replacing "overlap/must_stem_collision" in lib/specled_ex/overlap.ex left all 16 tests GREEN because branch_check.ex:38 still carries the literal. 22 of the 37 guarded codes appear in 2+ listed files and share this seam; the 15 single-occurrence codes are fully covered (confirmed with cross_field/affects_empty, which goes RED reporting 'dead in @known_codes').

Note this is arguably CORRECT union semantics rather than a defect — if branch_check.ex still lists the code in its severity defaults, the code has not actually left the implementation. specled_-vk0's stated failure mode (a code deleted from lib/ entirely) does go RED, so that ticket delivered what it scoped. Only pursue this if the project wants the deletion arm to detect per-detector decommission specifically, which would mean distinguishing 'emitting site' from 'referenced site' rather than unioning them.

ALSO WORTH FIXING WHILE THERE (cheap, cosmetic, from the same verification):
- Stale forward pointers to specled_-vk0 that will dangle once it closes: the moduledoc at test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:44 ('Deferred to specled_-vk0, not impossible') and the @token_patterns comment at :155-156 ('tightening the lookbehind bounds is tracked in specled_-vk0'). vk0 correctly declared the surface_target_/scenario_cover_ widening out of scope and did NOT tighten the lookbehind (A3 asked for boundary tests, not a tightening), so both pointers need retargeting or rewording.
- @known_code_list (:139) is dead indirection — introduced and consumed only at :142 to build @known_codes.
- @implementation_code_files is a new hand-maintained 10-file list whose own staleness is unguarded, though it fails loudly in the safe direction.
title: doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus ADR: four absolute stem-occurrence counts are stale; mirror union masks single-file code decommission
